ETH.note: The document describes a banking directive and a personal data law, not a national data policy.

facts.fact: The law firm Haymanot & Advocates says National Bank of Ethiopia Directive No. SBB/94/2025 requires all banks, foreign subsidiaries and branches included, to store and process customer and core banking data, primary and backup, within Ethiopia.
The same source says the National Bank of Ethiopia issued the Directive for the banks it licenses and that transfers of core banking data abroad need its prior written approval.

The law firm Haymanot & Advocates describes Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 as providing a comprehensive legal framework for collecting, processing, storing and transferring personal data, with which banks must comply.

The law firm Haymanot & Advocates says Directive SBB/94/2025 makes transfers abroad of non-customer data by banks conditional on National Bank of Ethiopia prior written approval, disclosure of destinations, adequate protection in the receiving jurisdiction and service level agreements.

The same source says Proclamation No. 1321/2024 permits transfers of personal data abroad only where the receiving country gives appropriate protection, the person consents explicitly, or the authority approves in advance.

ETH.note: The rules described cover banks' customer data, not government data or systems.
